text:
alex: Quick handoff — passing oncall to maya for the evening shift. Main item: planned release for routing-service -> v2.2. Deploy window 16:00-18:00 UTC, canary rollout + smoke checks. Freeze window 15:30-18:30 UTC (no infra changes during that time). Expected risk: medium (KV-cache warm-up latency spike + one flaky healthcheck on p-3). Auto-rollback enabled. Link to rollout doc: https://go/release/RS-v2.2

maya: Thanks — I'm primary pager. I'll set up the watchers and start monitoring dashboards 15:45 UTC. What are the explicit smoke tests to run after canary steps?

alex: Smoke checklist (quick):
```
# curl health endpoints
curl -sS https://routing.example.com/health | jq .status
# basic route test
curl -sS -X POST https://routing.example.com/route -d '{"src":"a","dst":"b"}' | jq .ok
# run smoke script on one canary host
./scripts/smoke/routing_smoke.sh --target canary
```
Also check p50/p95 latency on the "routing latency" dashboard and error-rate on the canary group.

sam: I'll be on standby for perf regressions. If p50 > 120ms or error-rate > 1.5% ping me.

ryan: I'll watch autoscaler and ingest pipeline. I checked earlier and autoscaler thresholds look sane, but I'll lower the scale-up threshold by 10% during canary as a safety net.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled for 2123460000. Canary plan: 10% for 10m -> 50% for 20m -> 100% over 30m. Auto-rollback triggers: error-rate > 2% OR 5xxs above baseline.

jordan: Infra FYI — we've reserved two extra hosts in us-west-2 for the rollout. No overlapping maintenance windows. If we need more, ping infra-oncall.

maya: Quick question: if rollback triggers, who runs it?

alex: I can initiate rollback until 17:30 UTC. After that infra takes over (see runbook). Rollback command: `releases rollback routing-service v2.1` (in internal CLI). Runbook: https://go/runbooks/routing-rollback

sam: If we see an increase in 429s during canary, first mitigation is to reduce edge concurrency:
```yaml
edge_proxy:
  max_conns: 1200
  concurrency_per_conn: 8
```
We'll coordinate config change with infra.

maya: I'll warm the KV cache post-deploy with a small traffic replay job to reduce cold-start latency. Command I'll run: `./tools/replay_kv_warmup --service routing --keys 50k`

alex: Leaving a note — watch for a known flakey healthcheck on p-3 instances (ticket #INC-4321). If it starts flapping, prioritize replacing the host rather than ignoring alerts.

maya: Got it. Starting watcher roster now: sam (prod perf), ryan (autoscale), jordan (infra standby). I'll @notify the channel at each canary step and post a final status.

sam: I'll hang around until 19:00 UTC in case follow-ups are needed.

ryan: same here. ping me on pager or DM.

alex: Thanks — handing off logs/notes in the release doc and enabling verbose tracing for first 15m of canary. Good luck! :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks alex — taking over. I'll post updates in this thread during rollouts.

deploy-bot: Canary started: step=10% scheduled at 2123460060.

maya: Seen. Beginning monitoring.

maya: canary 10% -> looks stable after smoke tests, p50 +3ms, errors normal. Proceeding to 50%.

alex: (post-handoff) ping if anything funky, I'm reachable until 17:30 UTC.

maya: 50% steady, no regression. Continuing to 100% per plan.

deploy-bot: Canary progressed to 50% at 2123460360. Scheduled 100% at 2123461200.

maya: 100% complete, running post-deploy full smoke and warming KV. All checks green. Closing watch in 30m unless alerts appear.

sam: Confirming metrics look clean. No rollout regressions observed.

jordan: Infra host usage nominal. Removing reserved hosts in 45m if all stays green.

maya: Thanks team. Ending active watch — will leave a final note in the release doc and follow-up if any degradation crops up. :white_check_mark:
